Nitrogen leaching-attenuation and indirect-N2O constants.

Source: R/datasets_balances.R
n_attenuation_constants.Rd

Scalar constants for the nitrogen-loss cascade: the input C:N leaching attenuation parameters (a_cn_*), the IPCC indirect-emission factors and the constants of the nitrate transport factors of calculate_n_leaching(). The C:N attenuation reduces nitrate leaching for carbon-rich, low-availability inputs; the indirect factors convert volatilised ammonia and leached nitrate into indirect N2O and set the ammonia-volatilisation fractions. swat_anion_exclusion is the SWAT anion-exclusion fraction of porosity; beusen_* and molar_gas_constant give the Arrhenius temperature effect on root-zone denitrification of the IMAGE-GNM method, and image_gnm_* its root-zone depth, the bounds its authors' model code places on the residence time and the temperature effect, the total runoff below which it moves no water through the root zone, the calibration factor of its surface runoff nitrogen and the four constants of its erosion slope factor. water_flux_floor_mm is the lowest drainage or total runoff accepted as a float residue of zero, shared by the Meisinger and IMAGE-GNM checks of calculate_n_leaching().

Usage

n_attenuation_constants

Format

A tibble with columns:

constant

Constant name: "a_cn_min_cn", "a_cn_span", "a_cn_span_other", "a_cn_max", "ef5_no3_to_n2o", "ef4_nh3_to_n2o_atl", "nh3_frac_synthetic", "nh3_frac_organic", "swat_anion_exclusion", "beusen_arrhenius_factor", "beusen_activation_energy", "molar_gas_constant", "image_gnm_tawc_depth_m", "image_gnm_crop_max_residence_yr", "image_gnm_no_drainage_residence_yr", "image_gnm_max_temperature_effect", "image_gnm_min_runoff_mm", "water_flux_floor_mm", "image_gnm_runoff_calibration", "image_gnm_erosion_slope_offset", "image_gnm_erosion_slope_range", "image_gnm_erosion_slope_intercept", "image_gnm_erosion_slope_rate".

value

Numeric value of the constant.

description

Human-readable description of the constant.

Source

C:N attenuation parameters from the nitrogen pipeline of an earlier regional historical reconstruction. Indirect emission factors and ammonia volatilisation fractions: IPCC (2019), 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Vol. 4, Chapter 11 (EF5 = 0.011 for nitrate leaching to N2O; EF4 = 0.014 for Atlantic, i.e. wet-climate, ammonia to N2O, p. 11.26; NH3 volatilisation fractions 0.11 synthetic and 0.21 organic, Table 11.3). Anion exclusion 0.5: the ANION_EXCL default of the SWAT Input/Output File Documentation, Version 2012, ch. 22, p. 304, as used in Neitsch et al. (2011), SWAT 2009 Theoretical Documentation, TR-406, eqs. 4:2.1.2 to 4:2.1.8. Arrhenius factor 7.94e12, activation energy 74,830 J/mol and gas constant 8.3144 J/(mol K): Beusen et al. (2015), Geosci. Model Dev. 8:4045-4067, doi:10.5194/gmd-8-4045-2015, eqs. 12-13, p. 4052. The 1 m depth of the total available water capacity: the same paper, eq. 14, p. 4052 (the top 1 m "or less if thinner"; WHEP has no soil-thickness layer, so the full 1 m is used). The cropland residence time of at most 1 year, the 100-year residence time without excess water and the bound of 1 on the temperature effect: the authors' IMAGE-GNM model code published with the paper, n_soil_denitrification.py (in N_model/trunk/tools/), lines 377-378, 179-182 and 97. The 3 mm/yr total runoff below which no water moves through the root zone: the same file, lines 341-344, with minimal_soil_infiltration = 3.0 (mm/yr) in parameters_history_100.ini, lines 203-204; the same threshold sets dry grassland and natural surpluses aside as inactive N in n_nowater.py, lines 31-46. The water-flux floor of -0.1 mm is assumed, unverified: the lower edge of the None bin of drainage_ranges, with no source recorded for that edge. The surface runoff calibration factor 0.3: the same paper, f_cal of eq. 9, p. 4052, and C_sro,N of Table 3, p. 4056. The erosion slope factor a + b / (1 + exp(c - d S / 1000)) with a = -1.5, b = 17, c = 2.3 and d = 6.1: the authors' code, n_erosion.py, line 50, for the soil loss of Cerdan et al. (2010) the paper cites on p. 4052.
